places.name: March of Pacified Borders
places.summary: The empire's frontier march, ruled by the Gongsun family of generals. Farmers plow with spears at hand, and every village has a watchtower and a beast-pit.
places.lore: The Gongsuns have held the march for nine generations and buried most of their sons on the wall. Every family owes one child to the garrison at sixteen. Rooted children are another matter: since the raids tripled, the Gongsuns hold a frontier charter, so the Registry's frontier tester comes at twelve, the age the march can put a child on the wall, and the garrison keeps every rooted child for its cadet school instead of sending them to the capital. Children here learn to read beast tracks before letters and to tell a raid horn from a hunt horn. A beast core turned in at a fort earns a bounty in rice or stones.

features.name: fields plowed with spears at hand

places.name: The Wall of Piled Bones
places.summary: A wall of earth and beast bones along the coastal hills, built over a thousand years of raids. On Ghost Month nights the bones howl.
places.lore: Each garrison adds the bones of the beasts it kills, and the oldest sections are faced with skulls the size of carts. Beast spirits haunt it in the seventh month, and ghost-hunters and bone-collectors come then. Old bones from the wall are a refining material for beast-taming whistles and Slaughter Dao artifacts, and stealing them is a hanging offense. The [[March of Pacified Borders]] garrisons the southern stretch, and its cadets learn the wall by patrolling it.

bone heaps waiting to be built in

places.name: Realm of Mingled Blood
places.summary: A shard world whose gate opens in a karst cave every seven years. It admits only those below Foundation who carry beast blood, or a tamer bonded to a beast.
places.lore: Inside is a green world where beasts and humans once lived as one people, with ruined villages, bloodline altars and herbs that awaken dormant bloodlines. Half-bloods go in to learn what they are; tamers go in to strengthen their bonds; pure humans who try the gate are thrown back with broken bones. The Night Bridge Society guards the cave and charges entry. It last opened five years ago.

features.name: the gate cave in the karst
a ruined village of the one people
herb meadows under a green sky

places.name: Soul-Lost Stone Forest
places.summary: A maze of stone pillars where a great python from the Vast Wilds Continent has made its den. Its illusions turn the forest into a trap no map survives.
places.lore: The Golden Python's grandson, a Nascent Soul serpent, crossed the strait six years ago and took the stone forest as its hunting ground. Its illusions make travelers walk in circles until they starve. Its shed skins are worth a fortune, and its den is said to hold the treasures of everyone it has eaten. Three imperial expeditions have gone in.

features.name: stone pillars that shift in the illusion

places.name: Kingdom of Spirit Herders
places.summary: A kingdom of beast tamers who raise war mounts for the empire from eggs smuggled out of the Vast Wilds Continent. The Beast Court has put a price on every one of them.
places.lore: The Kingdom of Spirit Herders's ranches raise thunder-horned deer, scale-horses and war hounds from eggs and cubs bought from smugglers. The empire buys every mount at a good price, and the herder families are rich, armed and hunted. Beast Court agents, half-bloods in its pay and now and then an old beast, cross the strait to kill tamers and free their beasts. Children are bonded to a hatchling at seven and grow up with it.

features.name: ranch corrals of thunder-horned deer and scale-horses

places.name: Kingdom of Stone Eyes
places.summary: Sinkhole villages in the karst, ruled by a council of cave clans. Half-blood families hide here, and nobody asks what is in the lower caves.
places.lore: Stone Eyes is named for the round sinkholes that dot its hills, each with a village around the rim and terraces down the walls. Its people farm in the sinkholes, keep bats for guano and guide smugglers through caves no map shows. The empire counts it as part of the march; the cave clans pay no tax and give no soldiers. Children grow up knowing which neighbors have scales under their sleeves and never saying so.

features.name: a sinkhole rim with terraces down the walls

places.name: City of the Guarded Mouth
places.summary: The fortress city at the head of the island chain, the empire's frontier headquarters. Its walls are faced with the skulls of beasts that tried them.
places.lore: The City of the Guarded Mouth holds the narrow coast where the chain begins, with a garrison of ten thousand and a bounty office that pays for cores by grade. Its markets sell beast parts, smuggled Vast Wilds herbs and frontier saber steel. Every sect with a frontier interest keeps a hall here. At low tide, the reef road appears below the walls.

features.name: the bounty office, paying for cores by grade
the reef road below the walls at low tide

places.name: Beast-Butcher Gate
places.summary: A frontier sect of saber cultivators who raid across the strait for beast cores. Brutal, rich and the beasts' favorite target.
places.lore: The Beast-Butcher Gate teaches Saber and Slaughter Daos and recruits frontier orphans who have already lost someone to beasts. Disciples earn rank by cores taken. The sect sells cores to the Apricot Grove Valley, hides to the Zhu clan's rivals and meat to anyone, and leads the empire's punitive raids across the island chain. It despises beast tamers as collaborators and half-bloods as vermin.

features.name: the drill yard, where rank is counted in cores

places.name: Night Bridge Society
places.summary: Half-blood smugglers who run the island chain in relays, one crew to a stretch, passing people, Gu eggs, beast cubs and herbs from island to island at low tide between the Morning Star Continent and Shared Roost City.
places.lore: The Society knows the tides, the reefs and which islands have something living on them this month. Most of its runners are Qi Condensation or Foundation half-bloods who know one stretch by heart, and each crew waits on its own tide, so a cargo takes about half a year to pass end to end; only the Core Formation leaders fly the whole chain, in about a month. It runs half-bloods out of human villages, beast eggs to the Kingdom of Spirit Herders's ranches, Gu to the marsh and Vast Wilds herbs to anyone. Its leaders are half-bloods with beast senses and long grudges. It pays tribute to nobody and has informers in every fort. Passage costs five low-grade stones, or a favor.

features.name: a tide pool island on the chain
